Best of 5 runs, wall-clock milliseconds, measured on Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8550U CPU @ 1.80GHz (8 threads),
Linux 7.3.3-200.fc44.x86_64, go1.26.10-X:nodwarf5. The record with the full machine context is
[`docs/bench/benchmarks.json`](docs/bench/benchmarks.json). The chart
beside it is [`docs/bench/benchmarks.svg`](docs/bench/benchmarks.svg).

| Scenario | Command | ms |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `startup-version` | `eka version` | 18 |
| `validate` | `eka validate .` | 26 |
| `sync` | `eka sync` | 45 |
| `view-execution` | `eka view execution` | 25 |
| `status` | `eka status` | 34 |
| `code-context-cold` | `eka code-context "context engine" --limit 8` | 222 |
| `code-context-warm` | `eka code-context "context engine" --limit 8` | 39 |
| `code-discover` | `eka code-discover "context engine" --limit 8` | 43 |

The two `code-context` rows are the same query. The cold row wipes the
derived cache before every sample, so it pays for walking and parsing this
repository's Go sources; the warm row answers from the cache that run wrote.
The index is paid once per source revision, not once per question. The
source tree stays in the OS page cache, so the cold figure is index cost
rather than disk I/O. These are one machine, named in the record — not a
claim about yours.
